Scenario Title: Cross-role availability consistency after booking
Primary Role: Customer plus Front Desk plus Hotel Admin
Entry Screen or Route: Public search, front desk dashboard, hotel admin room views
Preconditions: A room is available before the scenario starts and one customer booking can be created.
Test Data: Use a single room or room type with limited availability for the same date range across all three views.
Detailed Steps: 1. Create a customer or guest booking for a specific date range. 2. As front desk, review availability or booking presence for the same hotel and dates. 3. As hotel admin, review room status or room availability indicators for the same hotel.
Expected Result: Availability is reduced consistently across public booking, front desk, and hotel-admin views.
Evidence Required: Screenshots from each role showing the updated availability.

Scenario Title: Negative check for duplicate room sale risk
Primary Role: Customer plus Front Desk or two parallel sessions
Entry Screen or Route: Public booking flow plus operational view
Preconditions: Only one room or last available inventory remains for the target date range.
Test Data: Use a single remaining room or last available room-type inventory for the same dates.
Detailed Steps: 1. Complete a booking or check-in that consumes the last available room or inventory. 2. In a second session or role, attempt to create another booking for the same room or same sold-out inventory and dates.
Expected Result: The second attempt is blocked due to no remaining availability, preventing double sale or overbooking.
Evidence Required: Screenshots of the successful first action and blocked second action.

Scenario Title: Validate nightly subtotal and stay duration
Entry Screen or Route: Booking confirmation, booking details, or receipt
Preconditions: A booking exists for a multi-night stay with visible nightly rate and dates.
Test Data: Example values: Nightly Rate=ETB 2,700; Nights=2; Expected Subtotal=ETB 5,400.
Detailed Steps: 1. Open a booking summary or receipt with visible nightly rate and dates. 2. Count the number of nights between check-in and check-out. 3. Multiply nightly rate by number of nights. 4. Compare the calculated subtotal with the displayed subtotal or total room charge.
Expected Result: Displayed stay duration is correct and the subtotal matches nightly rate multiplied by number of nights.
Evidence Required: Screenshot of visible dates, nightly rate, and subtotal.

Scenario Title: Validate taxes, fees, and final total
Primary Role: Customer, Guest, Front Desk, or Hotel Admin
Entry Screen or Route: Booking summary, checkout receipt, or pricing summary
Preconditions: Hotel tax or fee configuration is enabled and visible in the chosen scenario.
Test Data: Use any booking where subtotal, tax lines, and final total are visible.
Detailed Steps: 1. Open a booking summary or receipt that displays subtotal, tax lines, and final total. 2. Record each displayed amount. 3. Manually add subtotal and taxes and fees, then subtract any displayed discount if present. 4. Compare the manual calculation with the displayed final total.
Expected Result: The final total equals subtotal plus all displayed taxes and fees minus any displayed discounts.
Evidence Required: Screenshot of the pricing breakdown and calculation notes.

Scenario Title: Validate refund amount after cancellation
Entry Screen or Route: Guest booking management or front desk cancellation flow
Preconditions: Refund rules are configured and a cancellable booking exists.
Test Data: Use a booking that is still within the refundable or partially refundable window according to the hotel rules.
Detailed Steps: 1. Cancel the booking using the normal cancellation flow. 2. Record any displayed refund or no-refund message. 3. Compare the displayed refund result with the configured hotel policy and the timing of cancellation.
Expected Result: The refund or no-refund outcome matches the configured hotel cancellation policy.
Evidence Required: Screenshot of the cancellation result and refund details.

Scenario Title: Validate currency formatting consistency
Primary Role: Customer, Guest, Front Desk, and Hotel Admin
Entry Screen or Route: Search results, booking page, confirmation page, receipt, and admin pricing views
Preconditions: Prices are visible in multiple parts of the application.
Test Data: Check ETB pricing in public search, booking summary, confirmation, front desk views, and receipt views.
Detailed Steps: 1. Review price displays in hotel search results. 2. Review prices on the booking page. 3. Review totals on the confirmation page. 4. Review totals on the front desk receipt or booking summary. 5. Review hotel admin pricing screens if available.
Expected Result: Currency is shown consistently in ETB, with readable separators and no conflicting formatting across screens.
Evidence Required: Screenshots from at least three different surfaces showing consistent currency formatting.
